about: When the President's opening address airs, as a clock time in one named zone; the opening day shifts it to the player's own place clock (read by src/director/address-airing.ts). And the share of a town's people who watch it live (read by src/director/address-audience.ts).

airsAtMinute.unit: minute of the day, Eastern clock (21:00)
airsAtMinute.source: NHPR, Feb 24, 2026, on that year's State of the Union: "The president is expected to begin at 9 p.m. ET., and if history is any indication, prepare for a long night." Joint-session addresses are scheduled for 9 p.m. Eastern; the spread runs from 8 p.m. (early starts) to 9 p.m.

watchedShare.unit: share of a place's residents watching the address as it airs
watchedShare.source: Nielsen's average television audience of the last two inaugurations against the resident population: 33.8 million in 2021 (Nielsen, Jan 2021: "An estimated 33.8 million people tuned in to watch the inauguration of Joe Biden", 17 networks, about 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. ET) over 331.9 million residents (Census Bureau, Dec 21, 2021: "the nation's population increased from 331,449,281 to 331,893,745") is 0.102; 24.6 million in 2025 (AP on Nielsen, Jan 22, 2025: "An estimated 24.6 million television viewers watched President Donald Trump's second inauguration", 15 networks, 10:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m. ET) over about 340 million (Census Bureau, Dec 2024: "As the nation's population surpasses 340 million") is 0.072. The value is their mean and the spread runs between them. Nielsen counts viewers aged 2 and up and leaves out streaming, so the share slightly understates who saw it live.
